doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: How guitar harmony helped his jazz violin
summary: He explains learning violin with no frets, using chord knowledge, and that jazz was not taught in school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And how did your guitar playing help you when you decided to play jazz on the violin?

Well on account of me knowing about the changes, chords and things, you know? And when I took my first lesson I could play better than the teacher but I didn’t know what I was playing so I still had to start over from, you know, C-D-E-F-G-A-D and down, and bowing all day and all of that. But it took me a long time to be able to play in tune, but being in my brother-in-law’s string band, he was just carrying me around, you know, and I played pretty close. You know I remember when my brother went into the service in the war. I believe it was 1918. [sings] How you gonna’ keep ‘em down on the farm.
Let me ask you. You say, you talk about the technique of playing the violin. Now unlike a guitar, a violin doesn’t have any frets.

That’s why it took me so long — me or anybody so long — to be able to play in tune, there ain’t no frets. But this is why or how the guitar helped me play the violin. Like I say, by me knowing that C-E-G was a C chord, and C-E-G and B flat was the seventh, and the sixth, augmented, whatever.
So that helped you to construct melodic lines along the confines of harmony. You actually understood the harmony rather than just playing individual notes.

Uh huh. All along. You know you play the melody, you know all the melodies. Well now they have the changes up over the melody. But way back you have to figure out the changes and chords yourself. And like the pianist, a pianist could be, a finished piano player could play anything she sees. If you asked her to make you a C diminished chord she didn’t know what you were talking about. They didn’t teach that.
That’s another thing I wanted to ask you is, so you basically learned by, well you didn’t study jazz in schools back then.
No, no, they didn’t teach nothing like it.
So how did you learn? © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
